extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, and examiner handling of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, including content, timing, signature, fee, electronic submission (eIDS), and how citations are considered and printed on patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements (37 CFR 1.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement shall be considered by the Office if filed by the applicant within specified time periods (37 CFR 1.97(b)-(d)). Examples: (b)(1) within three months of filing a national application (other than CPA) or before first Office action on the merits; (b)(2) within three months of entry of national stage; (b)(3) before mailing of first Office action on the merits; (b)(4) before mailing of first Office action after filing RCE; (b)(5) within three months of publication of international registration for international design. Later filings may be considered if accompanied by the 1.97(e) statement and/or fee (1.17(p)), or if filed on/before payment of issue fee with statement and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 609.04(b) and examiner checklist (MPEP § 609.01) for the table of time categories: (1) timely (within three months or before first Office action), (2) after (1) but before final/notice of allowance — requires 1.97(e) statement or fee, (3) after (2) but before issue fee — requires 1.97(e) statement and 1.17(p) fee, (4) after issue fee — IDS will not be considered. If bona fide attempt made but part omitted, additional time may be given per 1.97(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements (37 CFR 1.98) — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS filed under 1.97 must include: (a)(1) a list of all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted (U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications listed separately); (a)(2) a legible copy of each foreign patent, publication (or causing portion), each cited pending unpublished U.S. application spec/claims/drawings (or portion), and all other information or portion which caused listing; and (a)(3) for non-English items, a concise explanation of relevance and/or a copy of translation if available. Additionally, each page of the list must include application number; there must be a column next to each document for examiner initials; and a clear heading indicating the list is an Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)-(3) and 1.98(b) identifying details: U.S. patents by inventor/patent number/issue date; U.S. patent application publications by applicant/publication number/publication date; U.S. applications by inventor/application number/filing date; foreign patents with country/document number/publication or issue date; publications by publisher/author/title/relevant pages/date/place. Use PTO/SB/08 to ensure consistent format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification specifics for cited items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each category of cited item has specific identification requirements per 37 CFR 1.98(b): (1) U.S. patents — inventor, patent number, issue date; (2) U.S. patent application publications — applicant, publication number, publication date; (3) U.S. applications — inventor, application number, filing date; (4) foreign patents/published foreign applications — country/patent office, document number, publication date; (5) publications — publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required bibliographic fields are present for each listed item; missing or incorrect identification may cause omission from consideration or improper printing on patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and layout requirements for the IDS list
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS listing must have a separate section for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications, include the application number on each page (if known), include a column/space next to each citation for examiner initials, and include a heading that clearly indicates the list is an Information Disclosure Statement (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form PTO/SB/08 (encouraged) to meet format requirements and to enable examiner initials; avoid submitting PTO/SB/08 forms from other applications (to prevent confusing prior examiner initials and application numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and portions required to be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A legible copy must be submitted for: each foreign patent; each publication or the portion which caused listing (except U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required); for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and drawings or the portion causing listing; and all other information or the portion which caused it to be listed (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents are cumulative, one copy may suffice provided it is stated that the other citations are cumulative (see 1.98(c)). Copies need not be resubmitted if prior application is properly identified and relied on for earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120 and earlier IDS complied with 1.98(a)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English documents — explanation and translation
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-English documents cited, provide (i) a concise explanation of the relevance as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content, and (ii) a copy of a written English-language translation if such translation is in the possession, custody or control of, or is readily available to, any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise explanation may be separate from the specification or incorporated therein. If translation is available, include a copy to expedite examiner consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements under 1.97(e) — foreign-office citation timing certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under 1.97(e) must state either: (1) that each item was first cited in any communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the IDS; or (2) that no item was cited in a communication from a foreign patent office and, to the knowledge of the signer after reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing (37 CFR 1.97(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is required when filing outside the earliest time windows; incorrect or missing certification can render the IDS not considered. See MPEP § 609.04(b) for timing interplay with fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for late-filed IDS (37 CFR 1.17(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDS is filed after the periods in 1.97(b) and (c), it must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) under specified circumstances (37 CFR 1.97(c)-(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple eIDS are filed but only one fee is required, include fee with first eIDS and explicitly state on subsequent submissions that fee was included; subsequent submissions must be received the same date as the first submission to rely on the single fee (see MPEP § 609.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and formality requirements (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To have information considered, an IDS must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) (e.g., a separate signed page referencing and accompanying the IDS). An eIDS submission that complies with the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System will satisfy signature requirements (MPEP § 609).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a proper signature or authorized electronic signature is included. Examiners will accept e-signatures per 37 CFR 1.4(d)(3) for applicants and registered practitioners. Failure to satisfy signature requirements will cause the IDS not to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an IDS — applicant-only limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties (individuals not covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. Third parties may only submit patents and publications under 37 CFR 1.290 in applications published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) or file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291 for unpublished pending applications (MPEP § 609).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions not in compliance with 1.290/1.291 will not be entered into the application file and will be discarded. Third parties should provide information to the applicant who may then submit an IDS; Office personnel will not act on non-compliant third-party inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncomplying IDS placement and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.97 or 1.98 will be placed in the file but will not be considered by the Office (37 CFR 1.97(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should line through citations not considered and inform applicant of reasons. If none of the information listed complies, write 'not considered' on the IDS and notify applicant using form paragraphs (e.g., 6.49 series). A bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission may allow additional time to enable full compliance pursuant to 1.97(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligation to consider complying IDS and marking conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once minimum requirements of 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98, and 1.33(b) are met, the examiner must consider the information. Consideration means treating IDS documents in the same manner as other documents in Office search files during prior art search. The examiner should initial next to citations or use the alternative electronic signature method: stamp each page 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials and sign the final page (MPEP § 609).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should: (A) consider properly submitted IDS information; (B) draw a line through citations failing to comply and inform applicant why; (C) sign/date the bottom of the IDS listing or use the electronic method; (D) ensure a signed copy is entered into the file and mailed to applicant; (E) for eIDS use the eIDS icon and not require paper copies. Copy-and-paste of patent numbers to search tools is standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS handling in continued/continuing applications and RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules differ depending on relationship to a parent application and application type: (I) Information considered in parent need not be resubmitted for CPAs filed under 1.53(d); (II) For continuation, divisional or CIP under 1.53(b), information considered by Office in parent (other than international application) will be considered and need not be resubmitted unless applicant wants it printed on the patent; (III) For continuing applications claiming benefit to an international application that designated the U.S., applicant must submit an IDS listing documents cited in the international search report if they want consideration in the continuing application (MPEP § 609.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resubmitting, submit a new listing complying with 1.98(a)(1) timing requirements. Applicants discouraged from reusing a PTO/SB/08 from another application to avoid confusing prior examiner initials/application numbers. IDS filed before an RCE that complies with 1.98 will be considered after filing the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS in national stage (PCT) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In national stage applications, examiners will consider U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and U.S. pending applications cited in the international search report that are stored in IFW. Other documents cited in the international search report are considered when Form PCT/DO/EO/903 indicates copies are present in the national stage file; separate listing on PTO/SB/08 is not always required but may be necessary for printing on the patent (MPEP § 609.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wants international search report references printed on any resulting patent, a separate listing (preferably PTO/SB/08) should be filed within the set reply period. Use form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 6.53) to notify applicant when references were considered but not listed for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative disclosures — submission shortcut
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, a copy of one such patent/publication may be submitted without copies of the others, provided it is stated that the other patents/publications are cumulative (37 CFR 1.98(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly that omitted items are cumulative of the submitted item. This reduces unnecessary duplication of copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing of IDS citations on the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation listed on PTO/SB/08 and considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent. A citation in a separate paper will be printed if the list lends itself to easy capture by the printing contractor (single-line items, double-spaced lines, uniform format). Citations printed on the face of the patent will be distinguished from examiner-cited references on a PTO-892 (examiner-cited references marked with an asterisk) (MPEP § 609.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want pending U.S. application numbers printed, avoid listing them on PTO/SB/08. If classification info missing or incorrect, citation prints without classification. If a citation is considered but not printed, the file wrapper will reflect that fact (see MPEP § 609.05(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: eIDS (electronic IDS) submission rules and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS may be submitted electronically via Patent Center by entering citation information equivalent to PTO/SB/08 and transmitting it to the Office. eIDS may include U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and NPLs. Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not required; copies of foreign documents, NPLs, or unpublished U.S. applications not stored in IFW must be submitted as PDFs. An individual eIDS may contain up to 50 U.S. patents/application publications, 50 foreign patent documents, and 50 NPLs; multiple eIDS allowed (MPEP § 609.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one eIDS is necessary and only one fee is required, include fee with first eIDS and ensure subsequent submissions explicitly reference that fee and are received the same date. eIDS entries are scanned into IFW and linked to Patent Data Portal. Ensure accuracy of U.S. patent/publication numbers on eIDS because examiners will electronically retrieve cited documents (transcription errors should be corrected in a subsequent compliant IDS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic processing and examiner tools for IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office electronically processes IDS lists and provides examiners tools to annotate citations and electronically sign the IDS. Electronically processed IDS are stored in IFW as part of the official record and a copy is provided to applicant as part of an Office action (MPEP § 609.08).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners use eIDS icon to access and consider citations; they may electronically initial or use the 'All references considered except where lined through' stamp. Do not defer consideration of eIDS or require paper copies when eIDS complies with 1.97/1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS does not imply a search or admission of materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.97 shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made (37 CFR 1.97(g)). The filing of an IDS shall not be construed to be an admission that the information cited is, or is considered to be, material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56(b) (37 CFR 1.97(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need not conduct a patentability search to file an IDS; the act of filing an IDS simply makes the documents available for examiner consideration and does not itself concede materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification and form paragraph use when citations not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a citation fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.97 or 1.98, the examiner should line through the citation, inform applicant of the reasons the citation was not considered, and may use form paragraphs 6.49 through 6.49.10 (MPEP § 609.01(B)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where none of the information complies, write 'not considered' on the IDS and notify applicant. If a bona fide attempt was made with inadvertent omission, examiner may allow additional time to enable compliance and use form paragraph 6.51 where appropriate.
